findings.message: The fix dropped the old check that an adopted project's name and client match the opportunity. Now a resumed claim links whatever delivery project has that key. claimPromotion sets `resumed = true` whenever a stale claim has the same key, but it does not check that the claim actually created that project. promoteToDelivery then links `existing` without checking it either. Fix: record the project id on the claim once delivery creates it, and resume only that project. At minimum, put back the name and client match before adopting.
findings.scenario: Attempt A claims PS-0137 with key CRA. Its process dies before create, or its release `.catch` swallows a failure. A PM then creates an unrelated project CRA by hand for another client. More than 120 s later, someone promotes PS-0137 with CRA. The claim is stale and has the same key, so resumed is true, and existing is the hand-made CRA. PS-0137 gets linked to the other client's project and `presales.opportunity.promoted` is emitted for it.

findings.message: The 120 s claim is a lease that nothing checks against. A claim under another key is replaced if delivery has no project with that key yet, but the old attempt may still be creating it. Nothing stops that attempt's create from finishing later. Its recordPromotion then fails the token check and leaves an orphaned project. That is the same orphan the round-1 finding named, now reached through the timeout. Fix: re-check the claim token in the same transaction as the create (or right before it), or let the loser void its project. Add a race test with a create stub slower than CLAIM_SECONDS.
findings.scenario: Promote A (key CRA) claims, and delivery's create takes longer than 120 s. Promote B (key CRB) sees a stale claim and getProjectRef('CRA') is still null, so it replaces the claim, creates CRB and links it. A's create then finishes and makes CRA. recordPromotion rejects it with 'no longer claimed'. Delivery now has CRA with no opportunity linked to it.

findings.message: The round-1 finding about two opportunities sharing one project was fixed with the partial unique index `opportunity_project`, but no test covers it. review.test.ts only races one opportunity against itself. Add a table-driven test that links the same project id from two opportunities, both one after the other and concurrently, and through the resumed-claim path. Each must fail without the index.
findings.scenario: Remove the `create unique index opportunity_project`, and every test still passes.

findings.message: The untrusted text is gone, but so is any reference to the suggestion. Every 'Open in chat' button now sends the same fixed prompt, so chat cannot tell which find the user opened. The finding asked for the suggestion id, or a quoted data field, to be passed to the intent. Pass `s.id` as structured intent data, and have the chat intent load the suggestion itself as data.
findings.scenario: On the board, clicking 'Open in chat' on the Woodgrove Bank find opens chat with 'Opportunity from the inbox agent'. Chat has no client, amount or suggestion id, so it can't prefill or accept that find. The button does the same thing on every row.

findings.message: setTaskStatus and setRiskStatus now use lockOpenOpportunity, so tasks and risks on a won or lost deal can never be closed. No round-1 finding asked for this. Blocking new records on closed deals may be intended, but status changes on existing ones should stay allowed (or the open ones should be closed automatically when the deal closes).
findings.scenario: PS-0137 has an open task 'Send contract', due 2026-10-20. The deal moves to Won. setTaskStatus(PS-0137, task, 'done') throws 'PS-0137 is won; its records are closed', so the task stays to-start and overdue for good.

findings.message: `releasePromotion(...).catch(() => undefined)` swallows a failed release. The claim is then held for 120 s, and the next attempt is told the deal 'is being promoted right now', which is false. Log the failed release, or surface it with the original error.
findings.scenario: Delivery refuses to create the project and the release transaction also fails. A retry within 2 minutes reports a promotion in progress when none is.

findings.message: `taken_at` is stored so that a late snapshot is 'visible', but pipelineStats never selects or shows it. A late run still looks like the month-end figure. Either read and show it, or change the migration comment.
findings.scenario: The snapshot job runs on the 9th. The chart shows that figure as month-end, and nothing tells the user it is late.

findings.message: The promotion tests cover only two variants: the concurrent race with different keys, and a failed create with a retry. Three paths have no test. (1) The resume path that the docstring promises: the project was created, the link failed, and a retry with the same key links that project and makes no second one. (2) The stale-claim takeover with a different key, both with and without the claimed project in delivery. (3) The new unique index `opportunity_project`, which is the fix for the previous round's shared-project finding: no test promotes two opportunities onto the same project and expects the second to be refused. Add table rows that drive each case through promoteToDelivery or the services. Make each one fail when its guard is removed.
findings.scenario: Delete `create unique index opportunity_project` or the `claim.resumed` branch: every test in review.test.ts stays green.
